	// add a series to the data chart with the series name as the first argucment and an array as the second arguement

		let seriesObject = {};
		let description = title + ": " + seriesName;
		seriesData = convertSeriesData(seriesData);
		seriesObject = {name: seriesName, data: seriesData, visible: visible, accessibility: {description: description}};
		dataSeries.push(seriesObject);
	}

	// used when you have a mix of series such as line, column
	function addSeriesType(seriesName, seriesData, type, classColor = '', showInLegend = true, zIndex = 99 ) {
		let seriesObject = {};
		let description = title + ": " + seriesName;
		seriesData = convertSeriesData(seriesData);
		seriesObject = {name: seriesName, data: seriesData, accessibility: {description: description}, type: type, className: classColor, showInLegend: showInLegend, zIndex: zIndex };
		dataSeries.push(seriesObject);
	}

	// draws the chart and returns the chart reference
    function drawChart(container) {
   		let formatString = formattedTooltip;
		let tooltipHeaderFormat = tooltipHeader;
		let additionalTooltipData = additionalTooltipDataFormat;
	
		let chart = new Highcharts.Chart({
			chart: {
				polar: polar,
				renderTo: container
			},
			
			title: {
				align: 'left',
				text: title,
				useHTML: true,
				width: $(`#${container}`)[0].offsetWidth * 0.8
			},
			subtitle: {
				text: subTitle,
				width: $(`#${container}`)[0].offsetWidth * 0.8
			},
			legend: {
				enabled: isShowLegend, borderRadius: 5, borderWidth: 1, layout: 'horizontal', symbolWidth: 20,
				useHTML: false, itemMarginTop: 2, itemMarginBottom: 2, verticalAlign: legendAlignPosition, y: legendYPosition
			},
			yAxis: {
				labels: {
					enabled: enableYAxisLabel
				},
				min: yAxisMin,
				title: {
					text: yAxisLabel
				}
			},
			xAxis: {
				min: xAxisMin,
				categories: categories,
				labels: {
					y: undefined
				},
				plotBands: chartRecessionBands,
				reversed: reverse,
				tickInterval: tickInterval,
				title: { text: xAxisTitle },
				type: xAxisType
			},
			plotOptions: {
				area: {
					enableMouseTracking: enableTooltip,
					stacking: stacking
				},
				arearange: {
					lineWidth: 0,
					marker: { enabled: false }
				},
				bar: {
					dataLabels: {
						enabled: true,
						x: 50,
						align: 'right'
					}
				},
				column: {
					stacking: stacking
				},
				line: {
					enableMouseTracking: enableTooltip,
					dataLabels: {
						enabled: enableLastDataLabel,
						formatter: function() {
							if (this.point.x == this.series.data[this.series.data.length-1].x && this.point.y == this.series.data[this.series.data.length-1].y) {
								return '<span style="color: ' + this.series.color + ';">' + Highcharts.numberFormat(this.y, 1) + '%</span>';
							}
						}
					},
					label: {
						connectorAllowed: false
					},
					marker: {
						enabled: false
					}
				}
			},
			responsive: {
				rules: [{
				  condition: {
					maxWidth: 500
				  },
				  chartOptions: {
					chart: {
					  marginBottom: mobileMarginBottom,
					},
					legend: {
						//itemWidth: 100,
						verticalAlign: "top",
						//x: -15,
						y: 0,
						layout: 'horizontal',
						align: 'center',
						//verticalAlign: 'bottom',
						maxHeight: 50,
						itemStyle: {
							fontSize: '9px'
						},
						symbolWidth: 8,
						symbolHeight: 8,
						navigation: {
							enabled: true
						}
					}
				  }
				}]
			},
			series: dataSeries,
			tooltip: {
				enabled: enableTooltip,
				formatter: function () {
					let date = new Date(this.x);
					var s = "";

					if(tooltipHeaderFormat.length > 0) {
						s = eval(tooltipHeaderFormat);
					}

					if(formatString.length > 0) {
						this.points.forEach(function (point, i) {
							s += eval(formatString);
						});
					}
					return s;
				},
				shared: true
			}
		});

		
		
		let lastPoint;
		
		for(let i = 0; i < chart.series.length; i++) {			
          if(chart.series[i].data.length > 2 && typeof chart.series[i].data[chart.series[i].data.length - 2].y != "undefined" && chart.series[i].data[chart.series[i].data.length - 2].y=== null) {
                lastPoint = chart.series[i].points[chart.series[i].points.length - 1];
                lastPoint.update({marker: { enabled: true }}, false);
                chart.series[i].chart.redraw();
          }	
    	}
		
		let element = document.getElementById(container);
		let chartWidth = $(`#${container}`).width();

		// when a chart is inside a tab, the div width is the size of the tab header and not the full time
		
		element.style.overflow = 'visible';
		chart.source = sourceLine;
		chart.renderer.html('<div class="frba-highcharts-footer" style="width:' + chartWidth + 'px"><div class="source-line" >' + sourceLine + '</div><div class="frba-highcharts-logo"></div></div>').add();
		chartList.set(container, chart);
		
		
		return chart;
	}

function createSlider(
	sliderSelector,
	dataArray,
	chartInstance,
	defaultStart = dataArray.length - 1,
	getDateLabel = (date) => `${date[0].substring(0, 3)} ${date[2]}`
  ) {
		
	let start = defaultStart === dataArray.length-1 ? 0 : dataArray.length - defaultStart - 1;
	let max = dataArray.length - 1;

	$(`${sliderSelector}`)[0].setAttribute("default-start", defaultStart);

	$(sliderSelector).slider({
	  range: true,
	  min: 0,
	  max: max,
	  values: [start, max],
	  create: function () {
		$(this)
		  .find(".ui-slider-handle")
		  .each(function (index) {
			let pos = index === 0 ? start : max;
			let date = getDateFromArray(dataArray, pos);
			let label = getDateLabel(date);
			$(this).append(`<span class="handle-label">${label}</span>`);
		  });
	  },
	  slide: function (event, ui) {
		$(this)
		  .find(".ui-slider-handle")
		  .each(function (index) {
			let date = getDateFromArray(dataArray, ui.values[index]);
			$(this).find(".handle-label").text(getDateLabel(date));
		  });
	  },
	  stop: function (event, ui) {

		const dates = ui.values.map(value => getDateFromArray(dataArray, value));
		const labels = dates.map(date => getDateLabel(date));

		$(this).find(".ui-slider-handle .handle-label").each((index, label) => {
		  $(label).html(labels[index]);
		});
		  
		FRBAHighcharts.setExtremes(dates[0], dates[1], chartInstance);
	  }
	});
}

window.addEventListener('load', function() {
    const resetButtonElements = document.querySelectorAll('.dataPickerReset');
	 resetButtonElements.forEach(element => {
	// resets slider to beginning and end position
	element.addEventListener('click', function(event) {

		let id = this.getAttribute("slider-id");
		let $slider = $(`#${id}`);
		let defaultStart = $slider[0].getAttribute("default-start");
		var maxValue = $slider.slider('option', 'max');
		let values = [maxValue-defaultStart, maxValue];

		$slider.slider({values:values});
		// invoke stop to redraw the chart
		$slider.slider("option", "stop").call($slider, null, {handle: $slider.find(".ui-slider-handle"), values: values});
  	});
});


});	

/* Some dates are in 3/1/2025 format while others are in March 1, 2025 Format */

function getDateFromArray(dataArray, uiValue) {
	let date = [];

	if(dataArray[uiValue].Date == undefined) {
		// handle 1 dimentional array
		if(Number.isFinite(dataArray[uiValue][0])) {
			date = utcToArray(dataArray[uiValue][0]);
		}
		else if (!dataArray.some(element => Array.isArray(element))) {
			date = dataArray[uiValue].split("/");
		} else {
			//  handle 2 dimentional array
			date = dataArray[uiValue][0].split("/");
		}
		date[0] = monthNames[date[0]-1];
	} else {
		date = dataArray[uiValue].Date.split(" ");
	}

	return date;
}
	
function utcToArray(utc) {
	const date = new Date(utc);
	
	return [
		date.getUTCMonth() + 1,
		date.getUTCDate(),
		date.getUTCFullYear()
	];
}

// dates come in as either ["Month name", "dd", "yyyy"] or m/dd/yyyy
// the monthIndex is used for the max due to 3/31 needs to be 4/1 to show the first tick(far right) on the x axis
function convertDateToUTC(date, isStart) {
	let utc;


	if(date.length == 3 && typeof(date[1]) == "string") {
		date[1] = date[1].replace(/,/g, '');
	}
	
	if(Number.isFinite(date)) {
		
		return date;
	} else if(!date.isArray && date.includes("/")) {
		
		let dateArray = date.split("/");
		dateArray = dateArray.map(Number);
		
		if(isStart) {
			utc = Date.UTC(dateArray[2], dateArray[0] - 1, dateArray[1]);
		} else {
			utc = Date.UTC(dateArray[2], dateArray[0] - 1, dateArray[1], 23, 59, 59, 999);
		}
	} else {
		
		date[0] = monthNames.indexOf(date[0]);
		date = date.map(Number);
		if(isStart) {
			utc = Date.UTC(parseInt(date[2]), date[0], date[1]); 
		} else {
			utc = Date.UTC(parseInt(date[2]), date[0], date[1], 23, 59, 59, 999); 
		}
	}
	
	return utc;
}

window.addEventListener('resize', function() {
	// Clear the previous timeout
  	clearTimeout(resizeTimeout);

  	// Set a new timeout to execute the function when the user stops resizing
  	resizeTimeout = setTimeout(function() {
    	// This will be executed when the user stops resizing
		
		for(const [key, chart] of chartList) {
			const chartWidth = chart.chartWidth;
			chart.title.textWidth = chartWidth *.8;
			chart.subtitle.textWidth = chartWidth *.8;
			$('#' + key + ' .frba-highcharts-footer').css("width", chartWidth);
			$('#' + key + ' .source-line').css("width", chartWidth *.9);
			chart.redraw();
		}
	
	}, 250); // 250 milliseconds delay before executing the resize
});

function mdYToUTC(s) {
  // s like "1/1/1998" or "01/01/1998"
  const firstSlash = s.indexOf('/');
  const secondSlash = s.indexOf('/', firstSlash + 1);

  const m = Number(s.slice(0, firstSlash));
  const d = Number(s.slice(firstSlash + 1, secondSlash));
  const y = Number(s.slice(secondSlash + 1));

  return Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d); // month is 0-based
}

function convertSeriesData(series){


	if(series[0] && series[0].length == 2 &&  typeof(series[0][0]) == "string" && series[0][0].includes("/")) {
		const dateRegex = /^[0-9]{1,2}\/[0-9]{1,2}\/[0-9]{4}$/;

		if(dateRegex.test(series[0][0])) {
			
			series = series.map(([dateStr, y]) => [mdYToUTC(dateStr), y]);
	
		} 
	}
	return series;
}

function createChartDownload(chart, fileType) {
	
	const imageBase64 = 'data:image/png;base64,';
														
	const recMarkup = '<rect x="0" y="' + ( chart.chartHeight - 30) +'" width="' + chart.chartWidth + '" height="30" fill="#0060a0"/> ';	
	const imageMarkup = '<image aria-hidden="true" data-z-index="99" height="20" width="296" y="' + (chart.chartHeight - 25) + 'px" x="15px" preserveAspectRatio="none" xlink:href="' + imageBase64 +'"  href="' + imageBase64 +'"/>';

	const sourceMarkup = htmlToSvgText(chart.source, 15, chart.chartHeight - 40 );

	let svg = chart.getSVG(
		{chart: 
		 { width: chart.chartWidth, height: chart.chartHeight}
		});

	svg = svg.replace('font-size: 12px', 'font-size: 14px');
	svg = svg.replaceAll('font-size: 8px; outline', 'font-size: 12px; outline');
	svg = svg.replace('font-size: 8px; transform', 'font-size: 10px; transform');
	svg = svg.replace('</svg>', sourceMarkup + recMarkup +  imageMarkup + '</svg>');	
	
	if(chart.options.title.text.includes('Heatmap')) {
		svg = convertHeatmap(svg);
	}

	const blob = new Blob([svg], { type: 'image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8'});
	let url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);

	if(fileType != 'svg') {
		
		const img = new Image();

		img.onload = function() {
			
			const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
			canvas.width = chart.chartWidth;
			canvas.height = chart.chartHeight;
			
			const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
			ctx.drawImage(img, 0, 0, chart.chartWidth, chart.chartHeight);
			
			URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
			const pngUrl = canvas.toDataURL('image/png');
			
			if(fileType == "pdf") {
				const pdf = new jsPDF({orientation: 'landscape', unit: 'px', format: [canvas.width, canvas.height]});
				pdf.addImage(pngUrl, 'PNG', 0, 0);
				pdf.save( chart.options.title.text.split(' ').join('_') + '.' + fileType);
			}else {
				const a = document.createElement('a');
				a.href = pngUrl;
				a.download = chart.options.title.text.split(' ').join('_') + '.' + fileType;
				a.click();
			}
			
		};
		
		img.src = url;	
	} else {
		
		const a = document.createElement('a');
		a.href = url;
		a.download = chart.options.title.text.split(' ').join('_') + '.' + fileType;
		document.body.appendChild(a);
		a.click();
		document.body.removeChild(a);

		URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
	}
}

function convertHeatmap(svg) {
	svg = svg.replaceAll('class="heatmap-coldest-text"', 'fill="rgb(255, 255, 255)"');
	svg = svg.replaceAll('class="heatmap-colder-text"', 'fill="rgb(255, 255, 255)"');
	svg = svg.replaceAll('class="heatmap-warmer-text"', 'fill="rgb(255, 255, 255)"');
	svg = svg.replaceAll('class="heatmap-warmest-text"', 'fill="rgb(255, 255, 255)"');
	svg = svg.replaceAll('font-size: 7px', 'font-size: 11px');
	return svg;
}

function htmlToSvgText(str, x, y, lineHeight = 15) {
  const lines = str.split(/<br\s*\/?>/i);
	
	if(lines.length > 1) {
		y -= lines.length * 13;
	}

  const tspans = lines.map((line, i) => {
	  
    return `<tspan x="${x}" dy="${i === 0 ? 0 : lineHeight}">${line}</tspan>`;
  }).join('');

  return `<text x="${x}" y="${y}">${tspans}</text>`;
}

					chart.redraw();
				}
			}, 200);
		});
	});
});

					const id = this.getAttribute("id");
					
					if(id != null) {
						this.classList.add('btn-tertiary');
						this.blur();
						// 3-month button is clicked
						if(id == wgt3Month) {
							$('.' + topic12Month).css("display", "none");
							$('#' + wgt3Month).removeClass('btn-wgt');
							$('#' + wgt12Month).addClass('btn-wgt');
							$('#' + wgt12Month).removeClass('btn-tertiary');
							$('#' + wgtHourly).next('label')[0].innerHTML = "Hourly/Weekly Basis";
							wgtHighchart.setTitle(null, {text:"three-month moving average of median wage growth (hourly data percent)"});
							wgtHighchart.series[0].update({name: "Overall unweighted", data :  chart_overall, colorIndex: 0});
							removeAdditionalDemographics(checkboxElements);
						} else { // 12-month button is clicked
							$('.' + topic12Month).css("display", "inherit");
							$('#' + wgt12Month).removeClass("btn-wgt");
							$('#' + wgt3Month).addClass("btn-wgt");
							$('#' + wgt3Month).removeClass("btn-tertiary");
							$('#' + wgtHourly).next('label')[0].innerHTML = "Hourly";
							wgtHighchart.setTitle(null, {text:"twelve-month moving average of median wage growth (hourly data percent)"});
							wgtHighchart.series[0].update({name: "Overall", data : TwelveMonthMovingAverage, colorIndex: 0});
						}

						handleButtonClick(id, checkboxElements);
					} else {
						resetChart();
					}
				});
			});

			checkboxElements.forEach(element => {
				element.addEventListener('click', function() {
					removeSeries(checkboxElements, element);
					if(element.checked) {
						const movingAverage = $('.btn.btn-tertiary')[0].id;
						handleFilter(movingAverage, element);
					}
				});
			});

			filterElements.forEach(element => {
				element.addEventListener('change', function() {
					updateChart();
				});
			});
		
		}, 200);
	}
});


function populateDateFilters() {
	const startYear = chart_dates[0].split("/")[2];
	const endYear = chart_dates[chart_dates.length - 1].split("/")[2];

	let yearOptions;
	for(let i = startYear; i <= endYear; i++) {
		yearOptions += '<option value="' + i + '">' + i + '</option>';
	}

	$('#from-month').val(chart_dates[chart_dates.length - 1].split("/")[0] );
	$('#to-month').val($('#from-month').val());

	$("#from-year").append(yearOptions);
	$("#to-year").append(yearOptions);

	$('#from-year').val(chart_dates[chart_dates.length - 60].split("/")[2]);
	$('#to-year').val(endYear);
}

function updateChart() {

	const fromMonth = $('#from-month').val();
	const fromYear = $("#from-year").val();
	const toMonth = $('#to-month').val();
	const toYear = $("#to-year").val();

	let fromDate = fromMonth + "/1/" + fromYear;
	const toDate = toMonth + "/1/" + toYear;
	
	FRBAHighcharts.setExtremes(fromDate, toDate, wgtHighchart);
	
	for(let i = 0; i < wgtHighchart.series.length; i++) {			
            
		for(let p = 0; p < wgtHighchart.series[i].points.length; p++) {
        	let point = wgtHighchart.series[i].points[p];
            point.update({marker: { enabled: false }}, false);
		}
        wgtHighchart.series[i].chart.redraw();
    }	
}

function handleButtonClick(movingAverage, checkboxElements) {

	for(let i = wgtHighchart.series.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
		wgtHighchart.series[i].remove();
	}
	checkboxElements.forEach(e =>  {
		if(e.checked) {
			handleFilter(movingAverage, e);
		}
	});	
}

function removeAdditionalDemographics(checkboxElements) {				
	
	if(showAdditionalDemographics) {
		checkboxElements.forEach(e =>  {
			e.checked = false;
		});

		checkboxElements[0].checked = true;

		for(let i = wgtHighchart.series.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
			wgtHighchart.series[i].remove(false);
		}
	}
}

function resetChart() {
	for(let i = wgtHighchart.series.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
		wgtHighchart.series[i].remove();
	}
	$('.' + topic12Month).css("display", "none");
	$('#' + wgt12Month).addClass('btn-wgt');
	$('#' + wgt12Month).removeClass('btn-tertiary');
	$('#' + wgt3Month).addClass('btn-tertiary');
	$('#' + wgtHourly).next('label')[0].innerHTML = "Hourly/Weekly Basis";
	wgtHighchart.setTitle(null, {text:"three-month moving average of median wage growth (hourly data percent)"});
	wgtHighchart.series[0].update({name: "Overall unweighted", data :  chart_overall, colorIndex: 0});
	handleStaySwitcher(wgt3Month);
}

function handleFilter(movingAverage, element) {

	showAdditionalDemographics = false;

	switch(element.name) {
		case "wgt-stayer-switcher":
			handleStaySwitcher(movingAverage);
			break;
		case "wgt-industry":
			handleIndustry(movingAverage,);	
			break;
		case "wgt-full-time":
			handleFullTime(movingAverage);	
			break;
		case "wgt-hourly":
			handleHourly(movingAverage);
			break;
		case "wgt-wage-distribution":
			handleWageDistribution(movingAverage);
			break;	
		case "wgt-age":
			handleAge(movingAverage);
			break;	
		case "wgt-gender":
			handleGender(movingAverage);
			break;	
		case "wgt-education-level":
			handleEducationLevel(movingAverage);
			break;
		case "wgt-race":
			showAdditionalDemographics = true;
			handleRace();
			break;	
		case "wgt-census-division":
			showAdditionalDemographics = true;
			handleCensusDivision();
			break;
		case "wgt-msa":
			showAdditionalDemographics = true;
			handleMSA();
			break;		
		default:
										
	}
}

function removeSeries(checkboxElements, element) {

	checkboxElements.forEach(e =>  {
		if(e.name != element.name) {
			e.checked = false;
		}
	});

	for(let i = wgtHighchart.series.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
		wgtHighchart.series[i].remove(false);
	}
}

function handleStaySwitcher(movingAverage) {

	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Job stayer", data : chart_jobStayer, colorIndex: 1}); 
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name: "Job switcher", data: chart_jobSwitcher, colorIndex: 2});
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Job stayer", data : job_Stayer, colorIndex: 1}); 
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name: "Job switcher", data: job_Switcher, colorIndex: 2});
	}
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleIndustry(movingAverage) {

	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Services", data: chart_services, colorIndex: 1 });
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Construction and mining", data: industry_ConstructionMining, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Education and health", data: industry_EducationHealth, colorIndex: 2 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Finance and business services", data: industry_FinancialServices, colorIndex: 3 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Leisure and hospitality", data: industry_LeisureHospitality, colorIndex: 4 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Manufacturing", data: industry_Manufacturing, colorIndex: 5 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Public administration", data: industry_PublicAdministration, colorIndex: 6 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Trade and transportation", data: industry_TradeUtilities, colorIndex: 7 });	
	}	
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleFullTime(movingAverage) {
		
	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Usually full-time", data : chart_fulltime, colorIndex: 1}); 
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Full-time", data: UFTPT_FullTime, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Part-time", data: UFTPT_PartTime, colorIndex: 2 });
	}
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleHourly(movingAverage) {
		
	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Paid hourly", data : chart_paidHourly, colorIndex: 1}); 
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Paid hourly", data: PaidHourly, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Not paid hourly", data: NotPaidHourly, colorIndex: 2 });
	}
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleWageDistribution(movingAverage) {

	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "upper half", data: WageLevelHigher, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "lower half", data: WageLevelLower, colorIndex: 2 });
	}  else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "1st quartile", data: WageLevel1st, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "2nd quartile", data: WageLevel2nd, colorIndex: 2 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "3rd quartile", data: WageLevel3rd, colorIndex: 3 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "4th quartile", data: WageLevel4th, colorIndex: 4 });
	}	
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleAge(movingAverage) {

	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Prime-age", data : chart_primeage, colorIndex: 1}); 
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "16-24", data: age_16to24, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "25-54", data: age_25to54, colorIndex: 2 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "55+", data: age_55plus, colorIndex: 3 });
	}
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleGender(movingAverage) {

	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Female", data: chart_female, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Male", data: chart_male, colorIndex: 2 }); 
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Female", data: gender_Female, colorIndex: 1});
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Male", data: gender_Male, colorIndex: 2 });
	}

	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleEducationLevel(movingAverage) {
	
	if(movingAverage == wgt3Month) {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "College degree", data: chart_college, colorIndex: 1 });
	} else {
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "High school", data: education_HighSchool, colorIndex: 1 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Associate's degree", data: education_Associates, colorIndex: 2 });
		wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Bachelor's degree", data: education_Bachelors, colorIndex: 3 });
	}
	
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleRace() {

	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "White", data: ethnicity_White, colorIndex: 1 });
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Non-white", data: ethnicity_NonWhite, colorIndex: 2 });
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleCensusDivision() {

	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "New England", data: census_NewEngland, colorIndex: 1});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Middle Atlantic", data: census_MiddleAtlantic, colorIndex: 2});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "East North Central", data: census_EastNorthCentral, colorIndex: 3});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "West North Central", data: census_WestNorthCentral, colorIndex: 4});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "South Atlantic", data: census_SouthAtlantic, colorIndex: 5});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "East South Central", data: census_EastSouthCentral, colorIndex: 6});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "West South Central", data: census_WestSouthCentral, colorIndex: 7});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Mountain", data: census_Mountain, colorIndex: 8});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Pacific", data: census_Pacific, colorIndex: 9});
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function handleMSA() {
	
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "MSA", data: MSA, colorIndex: 1});
	wgtHighchart.addSeries({ name : "Non-MSA", data: NonMSA, colorIndex: 2});
	wgtHighchart.redraw();
}

function createStickyPriceChart() {
	FRBAHighcharts.initializeHighcharts("line", 180);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTitle("Wage Growth Tracker");
	FRBAHighcharts.setSubTitle("three-month moving average of median wage growth (hourly data percent)");
	FRBAHighcharts.setLegendPosition("bottom", -70);
	FRBAHighcharts.setMobileMarginBottom(130);
	FRBAHighcharts.setSourceLine("Sources: Current Population Survey, Bureau of Labor Statistics and author's calculation");
	FRBAHighcharts.setYAxisLabel("Percent");
	FRBAHighcharts.setPointStart(chart_dates[chart_dates.length-61]);
	FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Overall unweighted", chart_overall);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Job stayer", chart_jobStayer);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Job switcher", chart_jobSwitcher);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTooltip(tooltip);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTooltipHeader("'<span style=\"font-weight:bold;\">' + this.series.chart.time.dateFormat('%B %Y', this.x) + '</span>'");
	wgtHighchart = FRBAHighcharts.drawChart("chart-wgt");
}
function createMedianWageGrowth() {
	FRBAHighcharts.initializeHighcharts("line", 180);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTitle("Median Wage Growth");
	FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Smooth (3-month-average)", chart1_Smoothed);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Non-smoothed", chart1_NonSmoothed);
    FRBAHighcharts.setTooltip(tooltip);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTooltipHeader("'<span style=\"font-weight:bold;\">' + Highcharts.dateFormat('%B %Y', this.x) + '</span>'");
	FRBAHighcharts.drawChart("chart-wgt-median-wage-growth");
}

function createIndividualWageGrowth() {
	FRBAHighcharts.initializeHighcharts("line", 180);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTitle("Chart 1");
	FRBAHighcharts.setSubTitle("Distribution of Individual Wage Growth");
	FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("25th percentile", chart2_25thPct);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("75th percentile", chart2_75thPct);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Median", chart2_Median);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Average", chart2_Average);
    FRBAHighcharts.setTooltip(tooltip);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTooltipHeader("'<span style=\"font-weight:bold;\">' + Highcharts.dateFormat('%B %Y', this.x) + '</span>'");
	FRBAHighcharts.drawChart("chart-wgt-individual-wage-growth");
}

function createPercentOfIndividuals() {
	FRBAHighcharts.initializeHighcharts("line", 180);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTitle("Chart 2");
	FRBAHighcharts.setSubTitle("Percent of Individuals with Zero Wage Change");
	FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Median wage growth", chart3_MedianWageGrowth);
    FRBAHighcharts.addSeries("Zero wage change", chart3_ZeroWageChange);
    FRBAHighcharts.setTooltip(tooltip);
	FRBAHighcharts.setTooltipHeader("'<span style=\"font-weight:bold;\">' + Highcharts.dateFormat('%B %Y', this.x) + '</span>'");
	FRBAHighcharts.drawChart("chart-wgt-percent-of-individuals");
}

            <div class="intro-content">
                <h1 class="h1">Wage Growth Tracker</h1>
                <p class="leadin">The Atlanta Fed's Wage Growth Tracker is a measure of the nominal wage growth of individuals. It is constructed using microdata from the Current Population Survey (CPS), and is the median percent change in the hourly wage of individuals observed 12 months apart. Our measure is based on methodology developed by colleagues at the San Francisco Fed.</p>

Notes: (1) The size of the sample used to create the Wage Growth Tracker was 10 percent lower in November and December 2025 relative to September 2025, likely due to the decline in the <a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://www.bls.gov/cps/methods/response_rates.htm" target="_blank" class="link-external">response rate for the Current Population Survey</a>. The smaller sample size implies that the confidence interval for the point estimates for both months is wider than it had been. (2)  The three-month moving average calculations for December 2025 include September 2025, November 2025, and December 2025 observations because the October 2025 observation is not available, due to the missing month of data resulting from the federal government shutdown. The three-month moving average calculations for November 2025 include August 2025, September 2025, and November 2025. (3) Minor adjustments to methodology have been implemented to historical data from 2023 to 2025 with minimal impact to tracker measures.
</p>
							<h2>About the Wage Growth Tracker</h2>
							<p>
								The interactive chart displays the Wage Growth Tracker along with versions of the tracker for select work and demographic characteristics (shown as either 3-month or 12-month moving averages). See the downloadable spreadsheet for variable definitions.
							</p>
							<p>
								The Atlanta Fed's Wage Growth Tracker is a measure of the nominal wage growth of individuals. It is constructed using microdata from the Current Population Survey (CPS), and is the median percent change in the hourly wage of individuals observed 12 months apart. Our measure is based on methodology developed by colleagues at the San Francisco Fed.
							</p>
							<p>
								The Wage Growth Tracker is updated once the Atlanta Fed's CPS dataset is constructed (see the "Explore the Data" tab above). This is usually by the second Friday of the month. The exact timing depends on when the Bureau of the Census publishes the micro data from the CPS.
							</p>
						</div>	
					
					</section>
                    

                </div>
                <div class="tab-panel "
                     id="panel=2"
                     aria-labelledby="tab-2"
                     role="tabpanel">
                    <h3>Data source</h3>
<p>The data we use to compute the Atlanta Fed's Wage Growth Tracker are from the monthly Current Population Survey (CPS), administered by the U.S. Census Bureau for the Bureau of Labor Statistics. (You can find an overview of the CPS on the <a href="http://www.census.gov/cps/" class="link-external">Census website</a>.) The survey features a rotating panel of households. Surveyed households are in the CPS sample four consecutive months, not interviewed for next eight months, and then in the survey again four consecutive months. Each month, one-eighth of the households are in the sample for the first time, one-eighth for the second time, and so forth. Respondents answer questions about the wage and salary earnings of household members in the fourth and the last month they are surveyed. We use the information in these two interviews, spaced 12 months apart, to compute our wage growth statistic.</p>
<h3>US Census Bureau topcoding rule changes and the Wage Growth Tracker</h3>
<p>
Following the release of the April 2024 Wage Growth Tracker, changes to topcoding rules affected the Wage Growth Tracker. To thoroughly understand the impact of these changes on the data tool, we temporarily paused releases, resuming updates of the Wage Growth Tracker in July 2024. A Policy Hub: Macroblog post <a href="/research-and-data/publications/policy-hub-macroblog/2024/08/28/pause-and-resumption-of-wage-growth-tracker">discusses</a>&nbsp;changes in the underlying data and the implications for the Wage Growth Tracker.
</p>
<h3>Calculating hourly earnings</h3>
<p>The methodology is broadly similar to that used by <a href="http://www.frbsf.org/economic-research/files/wp11-23bk.pdf" class="link-external">Daly, Hobijn, and Wiles (2012</a>). The earnings data are for wage and salary earners, and refer to an individual's main job (earnings data are not collected for self-employed people). Earnings are pretax and before other deductions. The Census Bureau reports earnings on either a per-hour or a per-week basis. We convert weekly earnings to hourly by dividing usual weekly earnings by usual weekly hours or actual hours if usual hours is missing.</p>
<p>We further restrict the sample by excluding the following:</p>
<ul>
    <li>Individuals whose earnings are top-coded. The top-code is such that the product of usual hours times usual hourly wage does not exceed an annualized wage of $100,000 before 2003 and $150,000 in the years 2003 forward. We exclude wages of top-coded individuals because top-coded earnings will show up as having zero wage growth, which is unlikely to be accurate.</li>
    <li>Individuals with earnings information that has been imputed by the BLS because of missing earnings data.</li>
    <li>Individuals whose hourly pay is below the current federal minimum wage for tip-based workers ($2.13). </li>
    <li>Individuals employed in agricultural occupations (such as farm workers).</li>
</ul>
<p>These restrictions yield an average of 9,300 earnings observations each month.</p>
<h3>Constructing the wage growth tracker statistic</h3>
<p>Once we have constructed the individual hourly earnings data, we match the hourly earnings of individuals observed in both the current month and 12 months earlier. The matching algorithm results in about 2,000 individual wage growth observations per month. We then compute the median of the distribution of individual 12-month wage changes for each month.</p>
<div id="chart-wgt-median-wage-growth" class="highcharts-chart  margin-tb-xlarge">&nbsp;</div>
<p>The final step is to smooth the data using a three-month moving average. That is, we average the current month median wage growth with the medians for the prior two months. The chart below shows the unsmoothed and three-month average versions of the median wage growth series.</p>
&nbsp;
<p>Note that our matched dataset has a slightly greater share of older, more educated workers in professional jobs than does the sample of all wage and salary earners. This is primarily due to the requirement that the individual has earnings in both the current and prior year. Older, more educated workers are more likely to be continuously employed than other wage and salary earners.</p>
<h2><strong>Wage Growth Tracker by select employment and demographic characteristics</strong></h2>
<p>We also report Wage Growth Tracker measures for several job and demographic characteristics listed below (unless otherwise noted, the definitions refer to the individual&rsquo;s status in the current month):</p>
<p><strong> Occupation</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>High-skill: Managers, Professionals, Technicians</li>
    <li>Middle-skill: Office and Administration, Operators, Production, Sales</li>
    <li>Low-skill: Food Preparation and Serving, Cleaning, individual Care Services, Protective Services</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Industry</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Construction and mining</li>
    <li>Education and health</li>
    <li>Finance and business services: Finance, Information, Professional and business services</li>
    <li>Leisure and hospitality: Leisure, Hospitality, Other services</li>
    <li>Manufacturing</li>
    <li>Public Administration</li>
    <li>Trade and transportation: Trade, Transportation, Warehousing, Utilities</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Service Sector</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>In an industry other than construction, mining, or manufacturing</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Full-time</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Usually works 35 hours per week or more</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Job-Switcher</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>In a different occupation or industry than a year ago or has changed employers or job duties in the past three months.</li>
    <li>Note: Because the Current Population Survey is a survey of addresses, if a person moves to a new address they will be missing from the data. Therefore, job switching is defined only in a geographically local sense.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Paid Hourly</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Paid at an hourly rate in both the current month and a year ago</li>
    <li>Not paid at an hourly rate in the current month and a year ago</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Average Wage Level</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Ranking based on the distribution of average hourly wage in the current month and a year ago. Those in the lowest 25 percent of average wages are in the 1st quartile and those in the highest 25 percent of average wages are in the 4th quartile.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Age</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>16-24</li>
    <li>25-54</li>
    <li>55+</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Race</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>White</li>
    <li>Nonwhite</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Education</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>High school or less</li>
    <li>Associates degree</li>
    <li>Bachelor degree or higher</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> College Degree</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Has an Associate degree or higher</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> MSA</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) as defined by the U.S. Office of Management and Budget</li>
    <li>Excludes those whose MSA status is not identified</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Census Division</strong></p>
<ul>
    <li>New England: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Vermont</li>
    <li>Mid-Atlantic: New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania</li>
    <li>East North Central: Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin</li>
    <li>West North Central: Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota</li>
    <li>South Atlantic: Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Maryland, North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, District of Columbia, West Virginia</li>
    <li>East South Central: Alabama, Kentucky, Mississippi, Tennessee</li>
    <li>West South Central: Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Texas</li>
    <li>Mountain: Arizona, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Utah, Wyoming</li>
    <li>Pacific: Alaska, California, Hawaii, Oregon, Washington</li>
    <li>Puerto Rico and other U.S. territories are not part of any census division</li>
</ul>
<h3>Weighting Series</h3>
<p>Unless otherwise noted, all the series are based on an unweighted sample. The weighted series is constructed after weighting the sample to be representative of each month's population of wage and salary earners in terms of sex, age, education, industry, and occupation groups (irrespective of whether the person was also employed a year earlier). The weighted 1997 series is constructed after weighting the sample to be representative of the 1997 population of wage and salary earners in terms of sex, and age, education, industry, and occupation groups. These weighted series are described in two <em>macroblog</em> posts <a href="http://macroblog.typepad.com/macroblog/2018/02/weighing-up-wage-growth-tracker.html" target="new" class="link-external">here</a> and <a href="http://macroblog.typepad.com/macroblog/2018/10/demographically-adjusting-the-wage-growth-tracker.html" target="new" class="link-external">here</a>.</p>
                    

                </div>
                <div class="tab-panel "
                     id="panel=3"
                     aria-labelledby="tab-3"
                     role="tabpanel">
                    <p>The Wage Growth Tracker is the time series of the <em>median </em>wage <em>growth</em> of matched individuals. This is not the same as <em>growth in the median wage</em>. Growth in the median wage represents the experience of a worker whose wage is in the middle of the wage distribution in the current month, relative to a worker in the middle of the wage distribution 12 months earlier. These would almost certainly include different workers in each period.</p>
<p>Chart 1 plots the time series of the median, along with the mean, and the 75th and 25th percentiles of the individual wage growth distribution (all shown as three-month moving averages). The mean wage growth measure displays more variability over time than does the median. The mean wage growth uniformly lies above the median because the distribution of individual wage growth is asymmetric. The asymmetry can be seen by noting that the gap between the 75th percentile wage growth and the median wage growth is about 10 percentage points, whereas the gap between the 25th percentile and the median is only about 5 percentage points. Also note that the 75th and 25th percentiles have generally moved in line with the median over time, so that the interquartile range (a measure of dispersion) has remained relatively stable.</p>
<div id="chart-wgt-individual-wage-growth" class="highcharts-chart  margin-tb-xlarge"></div>
<p>One particularly interesting feature of the wage growth distribution is the proportion of individuals who experience no wage growth. Chart 2 shows the percentage of zero wage changes in our data (specifically the percent of individual wage growth falling in the range of +0.5 percent and -0.5 percent). For reference, also plotted is the median individual wage growth.</p>
<div id="chart-wgt-percent-of-individuals" class="highcharts-chart  margin-tb-xlarge"></div>
<p>Notice that the proportion of zero wage changes increased during both of the last two recessions. During the Great Recession, wage freezes became especially prevalent and have persisted at a high rate through much of the recovery. Only in the last year have we seen any notable decline in the percent of individuals experiencing zero wage change. For more information on this and its relation to models of nominal wage rigidity, see the work by our colleagues at the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco (Daly, Hobijn, and Wiles <a href="http://www.frbsf.org/economic-research/files/wp11-23bk.pdf" class="link-external">2012</a> and Daly and Hobijn <a href="http://www.frbsf.org/economic-research/files/wp2013-08.pdf" class="link-external">2014</a>). The distribution of individual wage growth is broadly similar to that shown on the <a href="http://www.frbsf.org/economic-research/nominal-wage-rigidity/" class="link-external">Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco website</a>, although the methodology underlying the construction of the individual wage growth distribution differs somewhat.</p>

<script type="text/javascript">
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
        const tabList = document.querySelector('.tablist');
        const tabItems = document.querySelectorAll('.tablist li');
        const tabPanels = document.querySelectorAll('.tab-panel');
        let selected = null;

        function activateTab(index, updateHash = true) {
		//Remove active state from all tabs
            tabItems.forEach((item) => {
                item.classList.remove('active');
            });
		    // Add active class to the selected tab
		    if (tabItems[index]) {
			    tabItems[index].classList.add('active');
			    selected = index;
                // Update URL hash if requested
                if (updateHash) {
                    const tabId = tabItems[index].id;
                    if (tabId) {
                        history.pushState(null, null, '#' + tabId);
                    }
                }
			    //Pass selected value to handlePanel function
			    handlePanels(selected);
		    }
	    }

	    function handleDropDownItems() {
		    tabItems.forEach((item, index) => {
			    //Onclick of an Li -->
			    item.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
				    // Activate the clicked tab
				    activateTab(index);

				    //Close the Dropdown
				    if (window.innerWidth < 1150) {
					    tabList.classList.toggle('drop-down-active');
				    }
			    });
		    });
	    }

        function handlePanels(selected) {
            tabPanels.forEach((panel, index) => {
                panel.classList.remove('active');
                if (selected == index) {
                    panel.classList.toggle('active');
                }
            });
        }

        // Initialize from URL hash on page load
        function initializeFromHash() {
            const hash = window.location.hash;

            if (hash) {
                const tabId = hash.substring(1); // Remove the '#'
                const tabIndex = Array.from(tabItems).findIndex(item => item.id === tabId);

                if (tabIndex !== -1) {
                    // Activate tab without updating hash (it's already in URL)
                    activateTab(tabIndex, false);
                    return;
                }
            }
            // No hash or invalid hash - activate first tab without adding hash
            activateTab(0, false);
        }

        // Handle browser back/forward buttons
        window.addEventListener('hashchange', function() {
            const hash = window.location.hash;
            if (hash) {
                const tabId = hash.substring(1);
                const tabIndex = Array.from(tabItems).findIndex(item => item.id === tabId);

                if (tabIndex !== -1) {
                    activateTab(tabIndex, false);
                }
            } else {
                // No hash - back to first tab
                activateTab(0, false);
            }
        });

        handleDropDownItems();
        initializeFromHash();
    });
</script>





    <div>
        <p>The Atlanta Fed's Wage Growth Tracker is a measure of the nominal wage growth of individuals. It is constructed using microdata from the <a href="http://www.census.gov/cps/" class="link-external">Current Population Survey</a> (CPS), and is the median percent change in the hourly wage of individuals observed 12 months apart. Our measure is based on methodology developed by <a href="https://www.frbsf.org/wp-content/uploads/wp11-23bk.pdf" target="_blank" class="link-external">colleagues at the San Francisco Fed</a>.</p>
<p>The Wage Growth Tracker is updated once the Atlanta Fed's CPS dataset is constructed. This is usually by the second Friday of the month. The exact timing depends on when the Bureau of the Census publishes the micro data from the CPS.</p>

        <script type="text/javascript">
            const COOKIE_NAME = "cookie_consent_session";
            let button = document.getElementById("scCookieBannerBtn");

            button.onclick = function () {
                // Setting the cookie without Max-Age or Expires makes it a session cookie
                document.cookie = COOKIE_NAME + "=accepted; path=/; SameSite=Lax;";

                // Hide the banner
                document.querySelector('.cookie-banner').style.display = 'none';
            }

            function getCookie(name) {
                const match = document.cookie.match(new RegExp('(^| )' + name + '=([^;]+)'));
                return match ? match[2] : null;
            }

            // If the cookie consent is found, hide the banner
            if (getCookie(COOKIE_NAME)) {
                document.querySelector('.cookie-banner').style.display = 'none';
            }
        </script>
